userStories.title: Classify outbound addresses and validate operator allowlist
acceptanceCriteria: Given every representative address in the blocked-range table (`0.1.2.3`, `10.1.2.3`, `100.64.0.1`, `127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`, `172.16.0.1`, `192.168.1.1`, `224.0.0.1`, `255.255.255.255`, `::`, `::1`, `fd00::1`, `fe80::1`, `ff02::1`, `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `::ffff:a9fe:a9fe`), when classifyAddress(address, []) is called, then it returns 'blocked' for every address.

Given each allowed edge address (`93.184.215.14`, `172.32.0.1`, `100.128.0.1`, `2606:2800:21f:cb07:6820:80da:af6b:8b2e`), when classifyAddress(address, []) is called, then it returns 'allowed' for every address.
classifyAddress('10.0.0.5', ['10.0.0.0/24']) returns 'allowed', and classifyAddress('10.0.1.5', ['10.0.0.0/24']) returns 'blocked'.
classifyAddress('not-an-ip', []) returns 'blocked'.
parseAllowedHosts(' Hooks.Internal. ,10.0.0.0/24,, fd00::/8 ') returns allowedHostnames ['hooks.internal'] and allowedCidrs ['10.0.0.0/24', 'fd00::/8'].
parseAllowedHosts(undefined) and parseAllowedHosts('') both return empty allowedHostnames and allowedCidrs.
parseAllowedHosts('10.0.0.0/33') throws an Error whose message contains '10.0.0.0/33'.
parseAllowedHosts('bad_host!') throws an Error whose message contains 'bad_host!'.
Given required variables plus WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS: '10.0.0.0/33', when validate() runs, then it throws ValidationAppException whose args has a WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS key.
webhookConfig() with WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS unset returns allowedHostnames: [], allowedCidrs: [] and deliveryTimeoutMs: 5000.

Given a testing module importing ConfigModule.forRoot({ load: [webhookConfig], ignoreEnvFile: true }) and ConfigBridgeModule with WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS set to 'hooks.internal', when WEBHOOK_CFG is resolved, then its allowedHostnames is ['hooks.internal'].

routing.reasoning: Cross-module boot configuration plus network address classifier; no authentication, token, cryptography, or role-check changes in this story.

modifiedFiles.reason: `envSchema` gains `WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS` with a custom rule that calls `parseAllowedHosts`.
gains a `WEBHOOK_CFG` provider and export built like `LIVE_CFG`.
provides and exports a `mockWebhookConfig` for `WEBHOOK_CFG` (empty allowlists, `deliveryTimeoutMs: 5000`) so DI tests that import `GlobalStubsModule` can resolve the new providers.

userStories.title: Guard webhook URL syntax, credentials and resolved destinations
acceptanceCriteria: OutboundUrlGuard.checkUrl('http://hooks.example/x') with empty allowlists rejects with OutboundUrlRejection whose reason is 'https_required'.
checkUrl('https://user:pw@hooks.example/') rejects with reason 'credentials_not_allowed'.
checkUrl('ftp://hooks.example/') rejects with reason 'scheme_not_allowed'.
checkUrl('not a url') rejects with reason 'invalid_url'.
checkUrl('https://2130706433/hook') rejects with reason 'blocked_destination', and the DnsResolver stub is not called.
checkUrl('https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/hook') rejects with reason 'blocked_destination'.
Given a DnsResolver stub returning ['93.184.215.14', '10.0.0.1'], when checkUrl('https://hooks.example/') runs, then it rejects with reason 'blocked_destination'.
Given a DnsResolver stub that throws an error with code ENOTFOUND, when checkUrl('https://hooks.example/') runs, then it rejects with reason 'unresolvable'.
Given a DnsResolver stub returning [], when checkUrl('https://hooks.example/') runs, then it rejects with reason 'unresolvable'.
Given a DnsResolver stub returning ['93.184.215.14'], when checkUrl('https://hooks.example/hook') runs, then it resolves, and the stub was called once with 'hooks.example'.
Given allowedHostnames ['hooks.internal'], when checkUrl('http://Hooks.Internal./hook') runs, then it resolves, and the DnsResolver stub is not called.
Given allowedCidrs ['10.0.0.0/24'], when checkUrl('http://10.0.0.5:8080/hook') runs, then it resolves.
Given a DnsResolver stub returning ['127.0.0.1'], when createLookup() is called with ('rebind.example', { all: true }, callback), then callback receives an error whose code is 'EBLOCKED_DESTINATION'.

Given a DnsResolver stub returning ['93.184.215.14'], when createLookup() is called with ('hooks.example', { all: true }, callback), then callback receives (null, [{ address: '93.184.215.14', family: 4 }]).

Given allowedHostnames ['hooks.internal'] and a DnsResolver stub returning ['10.0.0.7'], when createLookup() is called with ('hooks.internal', { all: true }, callback), then callback receives (null, [{ address: '10.0.0.7', family: 4 }]).

routing.reasoning: SSRF trust boundary with credential rejection and DNS rebinding prevention; security override requires isolated three-session TDD.

userStories.title: Validate create URLs and expose ADMIN-only webhook PATCH
acceptanceCriteria: Given a guard stub whose checkUrl rejects with OutboundUrlRejection('blocked_destination'), when WebhookService.create runs, then it throws ValidationAppException whose args is { reason: 'blocked_destination' }, and PrismaWebhookRepository.createWebhook is not called.
Given a guard stub that resolves, when WebhookService.create runs, then it calls createWebhook once with the given url.

Given a webhook in project p1, when WebhookService.update('p1', 'w1', { url: 'https://hooks.example/new' }) runs, then it calls checkUrl('https://hooks.example/new') before PrismaWebhookRepository.update.
When WebhookService.update('p1', 'w1', { active: false }) runs, then it does not call checkUrl and calls PrismaWebhookRepository.update('w1', { active: false }).
When WebhookService.update('p1', 'w1', { events: ['STATUS_CHANGE'] }) runs, then it calls PrismaWebhookRepository.update('w1', { events: '["STATUS_CHANGE"]' }).
Given a webhook whose projectId is p2, when WebhookService.update('p1', 'w1', ...) runs, then it throws NotFoundAppException and does not call PrismaWebhookRepository.update.
Given findById does not find the id, when WebhookService.update runs, then it throws NotFoundAppException.
When WebhookService.update succeeds, then it returns an object with id, projectId, url, events, active and createdAt, and no secret property.
Given a global ADMIN, when POST /api/projects/:slug/webhooks receives url 'https://10.0.0.5/hook', then it returns 400, and no webhook row exists for the project afterwards.
Given a global ADMIN, when POST /api/projects/:slug/webhooks receives url 'https://93.184.215.14/hook', then it returns 201.
Given a global ADMIN, when PATCH /api/projects/:slug/webhooks/:id receives { "url": "http://93.184.215.14/hook" }, then it returns 400, and the stored url is unchanged.
Given a global ADMIN, when PATCH /api/projects/:slug/webhooks/:id receives { "active": false }, then it returns 200 with data.active false and no data.secret.
Given a user who is not a global ADMIN, when PATCH /api/projects/:slug/webhooks/:id is called, then it returns 403.
Given the id of a webhook in another project, when PATCH /api/projects/:slug/webhooks/:id is called, then it returns 404.

Given the real i18n runtime (I18nCoreModule over src/i18n), when webhooks.-2 is translated with args { reason: 'blocked_destination' } in both en and zh, then each translation differs from the key and contains 'blocked_destination'.

Given a URL whose DNS hostname is unresolvable, when WebhookService.create or WebhookService.update checks the URL, then it throws ValidationAppException with args { reason: 'unresolvable' } and leaves the webhook uncreated or unchanged.

routing.reasoning: ADMIN access-control boundary and cross-project ID isolation plus API, database, translations and root OpenAPI regeneration; security override mandates strict TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the constructor gains `OutboundUrlGuard`; `create` checks the URL and `update` is added.
adds the PATCH handler for projects/:slug/webhooks/:id.

`new WebhookService(webhookRepo)` becomes `new WebhookService(webhookRepo, urlGuard)` with a stub guard; the existing create cases keep their assertions with a guard that resolves.

userStories.title: Deliver signed webhooks using guarded native HTTP transport
acceptanceCriteria: Given a local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1, allowedHostnames ['allowed.test'] and a DnsResolver stub returning ['127.0.0.1'], when OutboundHttpClient.post sends to http://allowed.test:<port>/hook and the server answers 204, then exactly one POST with the supplied body and headers arrives and post resolves.

Given empty allowlists and a DnsResolver stub returning ['127.0.0.1'], when post targets https://rebind.test:<port>/hook, then it rejects with WebhookDeliveryError.message 'blocked_destination', and the local server receives no request.

Given empty allowlists, when post targets https://127.0.0.1:<port>/hook, then it rejects with message 'blocked_destination', the DnsResolver stub is not called, and the local server receives no request.
Given an allow-listed URL whose server answers 302 with Location: /elsewhere, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'redirect_refused', and the server receives exactly one request.
Given an allow-listed URL whose server answers 404, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'http_4xx'.
Given an allow-listed URL whose server answers 503, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'http_5xx'.
Given an allow-listed URL whose server never answers and deliveryTimeoutMs 200, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'timeout' in under 1000 ms.
Given an allow-listed URL on a port with no listener, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'connect_failed'.
Given an allow-listed hostname whose DnsResolver stub throws with code ENOTFOUND, when post runs, then it rejects with message 'connect_failed'.
Given post fails with 'connect_failed' after ECONNREFUSED for allowed.test, when the error is logged, then Logger.warn is called once with text containing ECONNREFUSED and allowed.test.

Given an active webhook, when WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle runs, then it calls OutboundHttpClient.post once with the webhook url, a body equal to JSON.stringify(payload), and headers Content-Type: application/json, X-Koda-Event, X-Koda-Signature: sha256=<hmac of the body> and X-Koda-Delivery-Id.
When WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle runs, then it never calls globalThis.fetch.
Given a missing or inactive webhook, when WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle runs, then it does not call OutboundHttpClient.post.

Given the real WebhookOutboxSubscriber, WebhookDeliveryHandler, OutboundHttpClient and OutboundUrlGuard, a webhook whose url is https://rebind.test/hook and a DnsResolver stub returning ['127.0.0.1'], when FanOutPublisher.publish processes a webhook_delivery record, then it rejects and recordLastError is called with the outbox record id and exactly '1 fan-out handler(s) failed for webhook_delivery: blocked_destination'.

Given a previously stored HTTP webhook URL not on the allowlist, when OutboundHttpClient.post attempts delivery, then it rejects with WebhookDeliveryError.message 'blocked_destination' without attempting a connection.
Given OutboundHttpClient.post rejects with WebhookDeliveryError('http_5xx'), when WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle awaits it, then the same WebhookDeliveryError propagates unchanged.

routing.reasoning: Security-critical outbound trust boundary and preservation of HMAC signature; native HTTP/DNS/relay interactions and cryptography override require strict isolated TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the constructor gains `OutboundHttpClient`, and delivery goes through `OutboundHttpClient.post` instead of global `fetch`.

the assertions that global `fetch` is called with the method, headers, signal and body, and that a non-ok response rejects with `Webhook delivery failed with status N`, are replaced by the invariant that `OutboundHttpClient.post` receives the same URL, the same three `X-Koda-*` headers plus `Content-Type`, and the same body, and that a `WebhookDeliveryError` from it propagates unchanged.
the invariant that `WebhookDeliveryHandler` resolves with only a mocked `PrismaWebhookRepository` becomes: it resolves with a mocked `PrismaWebhookRepository` and a mocked `OutboundHttpClient`.

analysis: Existing Nest/Express API, Jest/Prisma monorepo; work is outbound project webhooks, not incoming CI/VCS webhooks. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.dto.ts:3-5 and :19-22 currently use @IsUrl, which accepts private IPs and rejects allow-listed localhost; URL semantics must instead be centralized in the guard while DTOs enforce string/2048 length. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.service.ts:9-23 stores URLs without validation; :25-53 implements existing list/remove/project lookup; guard injection changes its direct-instantiation tests at apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.service.spec.ts:31-38. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.controller.ts:23-36 already gates create with @RequiredPermission('ADMIN') and looks up slug; :38-69 has list and two ADMIN deletes, with the project-scoped delete ignoring slug (do not alter). New PATCH must resolve slug, verify webhook.projectId via service, check only provided URL, and return a secret-free WebhookView. apps/api/src/webhook/domain/webhook.domain.ts:3-23 defines WebhookDomain (includes secret), WebhookListItem (excludes active/secret), so do not return the repository entity from PATCH. apps/api/src/webhook/prisma-webhook.repository.ts:17-54 maps url/secret/events/active and :56-101 already provides createWebhook, findById, findProjectBySlug; inherited update suffices, with partial fields only. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-delivery.handler.ts:12-45 signs JSON body with HMAC-SHA256 and deterministic SHA256 delivery ID but calls redirect-following global fetch with raw network errors and status details; preserve exact headers/signature/id while delegating transport. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-delivery.handler.spec.ts:51-248 assumes fetch and needs replacement; apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.module.spec.ts:46-78 currently injects handler with repository mock only and must inject client mock too. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-outbox.subscriber.ts:13-20 registers the handler for webhook_delivery in onModuleInit; apps/api/src/outbox/fan-out-publisher.ts:13-20, :57-83 aggregates handler Error.message into persisted recordLastError and rethrows for normal relay retry, meaning only fixed delivery codes may cross this boundary, though the stored lastError includes the fan-out prefix. The prior payload-serialization error path in the handler also contains raw exception text; avoid leaking any raw delivery/socket text. apps/api/src/config/live.config.ts:6-34 establishes typed registerAs config conventions; apps/api/src/config/env.validation.ts:4-52 validates boot env and wraps Joi details in ValidationAppException args; apps/api/src/config/config-bridge.module.ts:6-60 globally exports typed config tokens; apps/api/src/app.module.ts:49-62 loads configs; apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts:70-99 must mock the new config token for DI tests. New outbound files do not exist. Use Node net.BlockList for classified IPv4/IPv6/mapped addresses and dns.promises.lookup(all:true) as a seam; check every DNS address both at registration and connect time to defeat rebinding, bypass DNS only for explicit allow-listed hostname, statically check IP literals because node:http skips lookup for them. Use native http(s).request with timeout and no redirects; log raw transport errors through Logger.warn once, never persist them. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.module.ts:12-25 wires existing providers; add resolver, guard and client in dependency order. apps/api/src/i18n/en/webhooks.json:1-4 and apps/api/src/i18n/zh/webhooks.json:1-4 lack -2; apps/api/test/unit/i18n/projects-translation-keys.spec.ts:19-49 demonstrates runtime translation. apps/api/test/helpers/http-app.ts:12-45 boots full global guards/pipes/filters; new route integration tests belong in a new test/integration/webhook file, not oversized endpoint.e2e.spec.ts. package.json:20-24 says root bun run generate exports the API spec and regenerates clients; openapi-ts.config.ts:3-5 points the generated CLI SDK to apps/cli/src/generated (gitignored), while root openapi.json is tracked and must be regenerated in US-003, making that story cross-root/package and therefore without workdir. No Prisma schema migration or existing-row rewrite: previously stored rows are guarded when delivered; security risk remains if custom lookup fails to validate every address, if an allow-listed hostname is treated like a CIDR/IP, if HTTP redirects are followed, if any unsafe URL reaches a socket, or if raw error text enters outbox. Failure/retry semantics remain unchanged, including retries for blocked destinations; operator allowlist is global, validated at boot, and affects both registration and delivery at lookup time.
outOfScope: Non-retryable delivery errors: a `blocked_destination` delivery keeps the relay's normal retry and backoff before it becomes `dead` (Slice 2a ruling 2026-09-27).
Inbound CI and VCS webhook hardening and the scope of `DELETE projects/:slug/webhooks/:id` (it ignores the slug today): Track 3 Slice 2b.
A CLI `webhook update` command and any web UI for webhooks: the PATCH route is exposed through the API and `openapi.json` only.
HTTP(S) proxy support: deliveries connect directly, and `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` are ignored.
Blocking NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`), 6to4 (`2002::/16`) and Teredo (`2001::/32`) prefixes: only the ranges in the Design table are blocked.
Re-validating or migrating existing webhook rows: rows created before this slice are checked at delivery time only.
Storing or logging response bodies: the body is drained and discarded.
A per-project allowlist: `WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS` is one global setting.

Extending `test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts`: it is past the 1000-line limit in `.nax/rules/api-testing.md`, so the HTTP-level webhook coverage lives in the new `test/integration/webhook/webhook-routes.integration.spec.ts`.

US-002 only: `createLookup()` called with `options.all` false. Node 22 and Bun 1.4.2 always pass `all: true` (spike 2026-09-27); the single-address callback form is implemented but not pinned by a test.
